development_rules: Follow SOLID, DRY, KISS, and Clean Code principles across all systems.
Use modular, component-based architecture with clear separation of concerns.
Use Entity Component System (ECS) architecture for performance-critical gameplay systems where appropriate.
Follow the project's established game engine, programming language, naming conventions, and directory structure.
Use strongly typed code and avoid unnecessary dynamic typing.
Keep classes focused, functions small, and responsibilities clearly defined.
Use dependency injection and interfaces to minimize coupling between systems.
All gameplay systems must be data-driven and configurable without modifying core logic.
Design all systems for extensibility, maintainability, scalability, and testability.
Use event-driven communication between loosely coupled gameplay systems.
Maintain deterministic simulation logic wherever reproducibility is required.
Separate game simulation, AI decision-making, rendering, networking, and persistence.
Implement AI creatures using modular behavior trees, utility AI, or state machines as appropriate.
Creature AI must support memory, learning, adaptation, autonomous decisions, and persistent behavioral states.
AI decisions must respect world rules, creature attributes, environmental conditions, and available knowledge.
Never use unrestricted generative AI directly inside performance-critical gameplay loops.
Use asynchronous processing and configurable update frequencies for computationally expensive AI operations.
Implement AI Level of Detail (AI LOD) to reduce simulation costs for distant or inactive entities.
Use spatial partitioning for creature perception, proximity queries, combat targeting, and world interactions.
Use object pooling for frequently spawned entities, projectiles, particles, and temporary effects.
Avoid unnecessary allocations, expensive searches, and blocking operations inside gameplay update loops.
Target stable 60 FPS on defined target hardware, with measurable CPU and GPU performance budgets.
Profile CPU, GPU, memory, and AI performance before introducing optimizations.
Use streaming, chunking, and level-of-detail systems for large open-world environments.
Ensure world generation and procedural systems support reproducible seeds.
Implement persistent world states with explicit versioning and backward-compatible save migrations.
All player progression, inventory, equipment, summoning, crafting, and economy operations must preserve data integrity.
Design combat, magic, progression, and creature systems around shared, versioned gameplay contracts.
All summoned creatures must follow consistent ownership, bonding, progression, and command rules.
Use server-authoritative validation for multiplayer gameplay, combat, inventory, trading, and progression.
Never trust client-provided data for authoritative gameplay or economy operations.
Implement secure authentication, authorization, input validation, and abuse prevention where applicable.
Design multiplayer systems to handle latency, reconnection, synchronization, and duplicate requests safely.
Use idempotent operations for transactions, rewards, inventory changes, and persistent multiplayer actions.
Use explicit error handling, structured logging, and actionable diagnostic messages.
Never silently swallow exceptions or hide failed operations.
All UI must be data-driven, responsive, accessible, and consistent with the game's design system.
Separate UI presentation from gameplay state and business logic.
Support localization through externalized text resources rather than hardcoded strings.
Use version control with small, focused commits and descriptive English commit messages.
Require code reviews for changes to gameplay, AI, networking, persistence, and security systems.
Write unit tests for gameplay rules, AI decisions, progression calculations, and data transformations.
Write integration tests for interactions between gameplay, AI, persistence, and networking systems.
Add regression tests for every confirmed bug fix.
Use automated formatting, linting, static analysis, and test execution in CI.
Never modify tests merely to conceal incorrect runtime behavior.
Do not introduce duplicate managers, services, utilities, or systems when existing implementations can be extended.
Avoid hardcoded gameplay values, magic numbers, unnecessary global state, and temporary workarounds.
Document all public APIs, gameplay contracts, architectural decisions, and important system dependencies.
Keep the Game Design Document, Technical Design Document, AI Bible, and implementation synchronized.
Check existing project documentation and dependencies before implementing new features.
Preserve backward compatibility unless a breaking change is explicitly approved and documented.
Implement features incrementally with clear acceptance criteria and measurable completion conditions.
Every completed feature must include implementation, appropriate tests, documentation updates, and validation evidence.
Do not mark development tasks complete until their acceptance criteria and required quality gates pass.
Never merge, deploy, delete production data, or perform irreversible operations without explicit approval.
Prioritize stable core gameplay, maintainable architecture, and consistent world simulation over unnecessary feature complexity.

risks.risk: Original multiplayer scope with a solo team
risks.mitigation: Stakeholder accepted risk. Sequence risk burn-down first (M1) with a formal GO/RE-SCOPE gate; architecture is server-authoritative from day one so nothing is rebuilt later.
Feature freeze per milestone; every new feature goes through Producer feature-request evaluation.

risks.risk: Godot performance for large open world + hundreds of AI creatures
risks.mitigation: M1 benchmark; data-oriented C# simulation core outside the scene tree; GDExtension fallback for hot paths.

risks.risk: Hardcore positioning puts us head-to-head with ARK/Palworld
risks.mitigation: Lead marketing with creature memory/bonding, not feature count.
Summoning contracts/rituals; legal check in M0.
Message as 'living ecosystem'; no generative AI in shipped content.
